refusal_note: No precheck (LEAD ruling): every refusal is one journaled invalid CP-DR step on attempt 0 of its own clone of the settled CP-0 store (the 'submission_against_empty_agenda' clone is the empty-agenda CP-0 store). The attempt is consumed, the result is rejected with limitations = the issues, and step_issues is the complete tuple that _verify_submissions replays exactly (S1a R3-2). The tool-use items (cited page read, absence backed by a search) are the core's RULES(text, seen) (G1-X protocol section 2; live/tools.py unread_citation_issues and UNBACKED_ABSENCE, product sorted order), called by G1-X at submit and in the verifier with rules='journaled'; RULES is pure over text and Seen and does not know pack membership: the two out-of-pack classes are one defect with both consequences, the membership issue then the RULES issue, in that order.

tamper.why_this_fact: the table cell holds the fact id and the step output holds the submission references, so the status lives only in the result Module; it is the one fact the probe's rebuild (bookkeeping over the journaled payload) contradicts
recipe: 1. Copy the closed partial store directory (blobs, snapshots, current, audit) to a scratch path.

2. Load the CP-DR head's result Module; replace only the text of fact TDR.1.missing-ownership-transaction.status; leave every other fact (TDR.1 questions 3, answered 2, unresolved 1, share 0.6667; every TDR.3.total.* fact), table, claim and limitation unchanged.
3. Serialise the forged Module as Execution._store does (model_dump_json); its sha256 R2 must equal Module.content_hash(); write blobs/R2.

4. Build a new ExecutionSnapshot equal to the current one with the CP-DR Attempt.result_sha256 and Head.result_sha256 set to R2 (status, inputs and commands unchanged, so head_of(forged Module) equals the Head) and the same parent; write snapshots/<its sha256>.json and rewrite current to that digest.

5. In the retained receipt: set the CP-DR SettledHead.result_sha256 to R2; set receipt.snapshot_sha256 and every coordinate that named the old final snapshot (the CP-DR settling OwnerSubmission.snapshot_after_sha256: owner_workflow.py _advance -> _finish_walk; its record is retained as audit/submissions/<content_hash> by _retain) to the new digest; delete audit/submissions/<old record hash> and write the edited OwnerSubmission as audit/submissions/<its content_hash> (model_dump_json bytes); rewrite audit/receipt.sha256 with the forged receipt's content_hash (S1a R3-5 and CP-3 A4 pattern: the audit file travels under its new hash).

expect.passes: everything upstream of the probe: audit inventory, blob and snapshot hashes, ancestor walk, head_of equality, begin and publication records, call and read replay, journaled-step replay (the payload and step are untouched)
expect.refuses: cpdr.probe raises WorkflowError('identity_mismatch'); verify_owner_run_receipt raises identity_mismatch
expect.test_asserts: on the forged copy, _verify_audit and every check before _PROBES pass (as CP-3 A4 (a)); then cpdr.probe raises identity_mismatch. A test asserting identity_mismatch alone would never show that the probe was reached.

tamper.step_output_edit: an edited CP-DR step output is caught by the store's own blob hash check, not by the probe's output comparison (recorded limitation, S1a R3-5)

tool_use.CP-DR: exactly one ok read_inputs per attempt before submit; ok search_pack covering every searched source of every question; ok read_pages for every cited locator; zero web or provider calls (no such tool exists); an invoke of any other tool is a refused not_permitted receipt
